title: Bunbun: a truth story
subtitle: How a comment travels from a browser island to an ATProto record

chapters.title: What Bunbun is
chapters.summary: A discussion service on the AT Protocol, with records as the source of truth and a local index for reads.

beats.title: Two sources, one conversation
beats.narration: Bunbun is a comment and discussion service built on the AT Protocol. Buns and threads are persisted as ATProto records, and a local index serves reads alongside the PDS source of truth. The index is a read model and a cache; it is never the place where a conversation truly lives.

anchors.label: What Bunbun is
anchors.excerpt: Bunbun is a comment and discussion service built on the [AT Protocol](https://atproto.com). Users authenticate with ATProto app passwords, buns (discussion groups) and threads are persisted as ATProto records, and a local index serves reads alongside the PDS source of truth. See [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) for the domain language (Account, Bun, Thread, Comment, Reply).

suggestedQuestions: Why keep a local index if the PDS is the source of truth?

beats.title: Three application surfaces
beats.narration: The repository is a pnpm workspace with three application surfaces. apps/api is the NestJS service, apps/web is the browser island bundle served same-origin, and apps/browser-acceptance is an opt-in Playwright tier. docs and plans hold the project's memory.

anchors.label: Repository layout
anchors.excerpt:
## Repository layout

Bunbun is a pnpm workspace monorepo:

```
apps/api                 @bunbun/api — the NestJS API (source, tests, migrations, configs)
apps/web                 @bunbun/web — the Svelte island bundle, served same-origin at /islands
apps/browser-acceptance  @bunbun/browser-acceptance — opt-in Playwright acceptance tier
docs/                    per-domain documentation
plans/                   project plans
```

beats.title: One glossary, shared by everyone
beats.narration: The domain language is explicit. Account, User, Bun, Thread, Comment, and Reply each mean one thing. A bun is a discussion group represented by an ATProto identity, a thread belongs to one bun, and replies nest inside a thread. The glossary is required reading before changing domain code.

anchors.label: Domain glossary
anchors.excerpt:
This glossary defines the project's domain language. It deliberately avoids implementation and storage details.

## Glossary

### Account

An AT Protocol identity that can authenticate and own records. Use a more specific term when the role is known: **user account** for a person using Bunbun, **bun account** for a discussion group, and **example account** for the ALICE or BOB identities used by the demo.

chapters.title: From request to page
chapters.summary: How a thread page is assembled from a loader, a query, and the local index without turning the controller into the application.

beats.title: Boot is one explicit path
beats.narration: Boot starts in main.ts. It loads the environment, creates the Nest application, installs static mounts, a global validation pipe, exception filters, and a graceful shutdown path. The app fails fast when required configuration is missing, so a broken environment never pretends to be healthy.

anchors.label: bootstrap()

beats.title: AppModule is the wiring seam
beats.narration: AppModule imports the feature modules that make up the service: accounts, comments, buns, threads, moderation, sync, tags, telemetry, and the rest. It also registers the global interceptor and the exception filters in a deliberate order, because filter precedence is behavior, not decoration.

anchors.label: AppModule imports

beats.title: The page controller is a thin adapter
beats.narration: The public thread page is a thin adapter. The controller parses the request, applies security headers, asks ThreadPageLoader for one page state, and renders it. It does not know how comments, moderation, tags, or revisions are fetched, which is what keeps the page shape testable.

anchors.label: ThreadCommentsPageController

beats.title: The loader returns named page states
beats.narration: ThreadPageLoader resolves the thread, the bun, the viewer, the moderation context, the comment tree, revisions, tags, and viewer relations. It returns a discriminated union of page states, so not-found, taken-down, labeled, age-gated, and error pages each have a name instead of collapsing into one vague message.

anchors.label: ThreadPageLoader
Page-state union

beats.title: The query owns the read model
beats.narration: CommentThreadQuery is the read model. It fetches a thread's records, resolves moderation state for the viewer in front of it, orders root comments, and walks replies into a tree. The local index is consulted first, and the PDS covers unknown or legacy entries. The query composes the conversation; it does not render it.

anchors.label: CommentThreadQuery

chapters.title: From comment to record
chapters.summary: Identity, validation, the PDS write, the local index upsert, and the single writer that invalidates caches.

beats.title: Identity comes from proof, not from input
beats.narration: Writes begin with identity. OAuthSessionGuard restores the persisted OAuth session, resolves the author, and attaches that author to the request. Downstream code never accepts an author from the request body, which is the difference between an authenticated write and a hopeful one.

anchors.label: OAuthSessionGuard

beats.title: The service orders the write
beats.narration: CommentsService.create validates the text, thread, and parent, computes the root, calls the PDS adapter, then upserts the local index. The author came from the guard; the service does not re-derive it from the payload. The order matters: the record exists before the index claims it does.

anchors.label: CommentsService.create

beats.title: The adapter is the PDS seam
beats.narration: AtprotoCommentPdsAdapter.create builds the ATProto record with the thread, parent, root, author, and timestamps, then calls com.atproto.repo.createRecord on the author's agent. The adapter is the only place that knows the collection name and the repository call, which keeps the PDS shape out of the service.

anchors.label: AtprotoCommentPdsAdapter.create

beats.title: One writer invalidates the cache
beats.narration: IndexWriter is the single write path for the local index. Each write invalidates the affected cache shape before the write resolves, so a reader never sees a stale shape after a successful mutation. Comments, threads, and tags all ride the same writer, which is how invalidation stays honest across features.

anchors.label: IndexWriter

chapters.title: Keeping the index honest
chapters.summary: The worker thread, the reconcilers, and the cross-cutting tag service that keep local state in step with the PDS.

beats.title: The worker owns the writes
beats.narration: The sync worker runs in its own thread with its own Prisma client. It owns the IndexWriter, posts invalidation events to the main process, and runs the reconcilers. That is why the worker never touches the main process's read-through cache: it has no request context and no business seeing another thread's memory.

anchors.label: Sync worker entry

beats.title: Reconcile is a bounded batch
beats.narration: ThreadReconciler lists a bun's thread records from the PDS and hands them to the writer's reconcile. A bun whose credentials vanished is skipped, so one unreadable bun does not stop the rest of the batch. Each step is timed and reported, which is how a background loop becomes observable instead of mysterious.

anchors.label: ThreadReconciler

beats.title: Tags are a hub, not a controller
beats.narration: TagService resolves the actor's standing, writes the repository record or local audit row through the index write seam, and keeps the tag index in step. It is a hub of ports, not a controller. That shape is what lets tags, moderation, and the index share one write path without importing each other's modules.

anchors.label: TagService

chapters.title: The browser island
chapters.summary: One bundle, a data-island registry, and the comment composer that keeps drafts alive across sessions.

beats.title: One bundle, named islands
beats.narration: The web client is one Svelte island bundle. main.ts maps data-island names to components and mounts them; unknown island names are ignored, so a stale cached bundle never breaks a newer page. There is no per-page script wiring and no client-side router standing between the reader and the HTML.

anchors.label: Island registry

beats.title: A draft that survives the session
beats.narration: The comment composer keeps a sessionStorage mirror and a server copy of the draft, then reconciles newer-wins so a failed request never loses the later edit. Preview goes through the server's sanitization pipeline, and the reply composer floats with keyboard controls as the primary path.

anchors.label: CommentComposer
anchors.excerpt:
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';
  import {
    apiFetch,
    clearDraft,
    getComposerLayout,
    getDraft,
    saveComposerLayout,
    saveDraft,
  } from '../../lib/api.js';

  let {
    threadLocalId,
    parentId = '',
    maxLength,
  }: {
    threadLocalId?: string;
    parentId?: string;
    // The comment-text bound from the server's mount payload (Phase 9 B4,
    // `data-max-length` in thread-page-render.ts, source constant
    // apps/api/src/comments/comment-limits.ts). Why a prop and not a literal:
    // the number exists once on the server; if a future page forgot the
    // attribute, the textarea simply loses its client-side cap and the API's
    // 400 message stays the single enforcement point.
    maxLength?: string;
  } = $props();

  /** Idle window before a keystroke is written to the server; long enough to coalesce typing, short enough to survive a crash. */
  const DRAFT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 500;
  /** The responsive baseline breakpoint (shared `main` is max-width: 760px); below it the reply box docks. */
  const MOBILE_BREAKPOINT_QUERY = '(max-width: 760px)';
  const ROOT_PARENT_KEY = 'root';
  const MOVE_STEP = 10;
  const MIN_BOX_WIDTH = 220;
  const MIN_BOX_HEIGHT = 140;

  const draftKey = `bunbun-draft-${threadLocalId ?? ''}-${parentId || ROOT_PARENT_KEY}`;
  const fieldId = `comment-text-${parentId || ROOT_PARENT_KEY}`;
  /** Only the reply instance floats; the root composer is the inline form. */
  const floating = $derived(Boolean(parentId));

beats.title: The docs index is the map
beats.narration: The documentation index is the canonical map of the project. It lists feature guides for accounts, buns, comments, threads, preferences, and feeds, and cross-cutting guides for admin, moderation, cache and sync, identity, accessibility, and the browser tier. When behavior changes, the relevant guide changes with it.

beats.title: Verification is part of the change
beats.narration: To extend Bunbun, add a feature module, wire it in AppModule, add a page or island, and verify it with the project's own commands. Typecheck, lint, the unit suite, the browser tier, and the canonical dev server are not optional ceremony. They are how the next reader can trust the story you just told.

anchors.label: Project commands
anchors.excerpt:
## Commands

- Install: `pnpm install`. Setup, env keys, and the devnet overlay are documented in [README.md](README.md).
- All scripts below run from the repo root (root `package.json` delegates to `@bunbun/api` via `pnpm --filter`) or from `apps/api/`; the devnet command's `./data/root.crt` resolves against `apps/api/data/`.
- Dev server, internet profile (the canonical verification command): `PORT=3001 pnpm start:dev` — runs against the public ATProto network, no CA or devnet env needed.
- Dev server, devnet profile: `PORT=3001 pnpm start:localdev` — sets `ATPROTO_ENV=localdev` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=./data/root.crt` itself, and requires the atmosphereinabox sandbox plus a `.env.localdev` overlay (see [README.md](README.md)).
- Dev server ports are 3001–3003. An agent may always kill any process listening on one of those ports to free it: the developer never starts the dev server by hand while an agent is working, so processes on those ports are safe to stop (restart the canonical command afterwards).
- Lint: `pnpm lint` (oxlint with type-aware rules) · Format: `pnpm format`
- Web island bundle: `pnpm --filter @bunbun/web build` (emits `apps/web/dist` + vite manifest, served at `/islands`) · `pnpm --filter @bunbun/web test` (its vitest suite). Not required for the API to boot — a missing build is skipped gracefully.
- Unit tests: `pnpm --filter @bunbun/api exec vitest run <relevant-path>` (or `pnpm test` for the full suite). The default config matches only `**/*.spec.ts` (colocated specs).
- E2E tests: `pnpm test:e2e` (config matches `**/*.e2e-spec.ts`).
- Browser acceptance (Playwright, opt-in): `pnpm test:browser` — needs a running server (`127.0.0.1:3001`) and, for the authenticated specs, the atmosphereinabox devnet; skips cleanly when the devnet is down. Comment-writing spec is opt-in via `BUNBUN_ACCEPTANCE_ALLOW_WRITES=1`. See `docs/browser-acceptance.md`.
- Database contract changes: `pnpm contract:emit && pnpm contract:patch-types` (see below).
- Local ATProto sandbox: driven by `deno task sandbox ...` in the separate atmosphereinabox project (see [README.md](README.md)).
